deities: Goddess Mariamman (Samayapurathal) - swayambhu (self-manifested); the idol is made of sand and clay, so no liquid abhishekams are performed
Sub-deities: Lord Mahadeva, Subramanya, Bhairava, Ayyanar, Kailasanathar, Virabhadra
festivals: Poochoriyal (Flower Sprinkling Festival) - 28 days in the Tamil month of Masi, marking the end of the Goddess's 28-day fast; the deity is bathed only with flowers
Chithirai Festival - 13 days across Chithirai-Panguni, with a chariot procession
Navaratri - 9 days in Purattasi; also Panguni Uthiram celebrations

CSV TOWN FLAG: the CSV lists the town as Tiruchirappalli, but the temple stands at SAMAYAPURAM village on NH-45, roughly 11-15 km north of Tiruchirappalli city (sources vary between 10 and 24 km). Its historical name is Kannapuram. This swayambhu Mariamman shrine is one of Tamil Nadu's wealthiest temples under the HRCE Department. The goddess is worshipped for health, fertility and protection; devotees offer small metallic figurines praying for cures from illness, and women offer mangalyams (thalis) to the hundi. Signature practice: a 28-day fast by the Goddess from the last Sunday of Maasi (only fruits and flour offered), ending in the Poo Choriyal flower abhishekam. Devotees perform Anga Pradakshinam (rolling through the prakaram in wet clothes). The neem tree is the thala virutcham.

name: Samayapuram Mariamman Temple
town_description: Samayapuram is a village and pilgrimage town in Tiruchirappalli district on National Highway NH-45 (PIN 621112), roughly 11-15 km north of Tiruchirappalli city. It exists almost entirely around the famous Mariamman temple that draws devotees from across Tamil Nadu and beyond.

travel.railway: Tiruchirappalli Junction is the main railhead; the temple is about 15 km from the city.
travel.road: On NH-45 at Samayapuram; Srirangam is about 10 km away, Rockfort Temple about 13-14 km; frequent buses from Tiruchirappalli.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March. The 28-day Poochoriyal (Masi) and Thai Poosam are the grandest festivals - expect very heavy crowds.
